subject.title: fix(qqbot): allow approval buttons in direct C2C conversations

question: Which identity must authorize a QQBot C2C fallback approval: the original request sender or recipient, a configured approval owner, or the existing explicit non-wildcard command allowlist?
rationale: Choosing the authoritative approver changes the documented security model; an open DM conversation identifies the chatting QQ user but does not establish that the user owns the bot or may approve sensitive operations.

options.title: Bind the request user
options.body: Record the originating C2C user OpenID with the approval and accept only that same user's callback while retaining group authorization.

options.title: Keep explicit approvers
options.body: Preserve the current allowlist or exec-approval approver requirement and improve rejection and setup guidance for affected users.

options.title: Trust every C2C sender
options.body: Adopt unconditional direct-chat authorization and explicitly document that open DM access also grants fallback approval authority.

recommendation.title: Bind the request user
recommendation.body: Record the originating C2C user OpenID with the approval and accept only that same user's callback while retaining group authorization.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work most directly established the current fallback actor authorization contract and tests.
